replacements.before:
Table~\ref{tab:process-dynamics} shows that one \texttt{Planning}$\rightarrow$\texttt{Translating}$\rightarrow$\texttt{Reviewing} cycle dominates the traces; returning to planning after review and replacing an existing goal are both rare.
Our system therefore has the ability to revisit earlier processes but uses that flexibility infrequently on the evaluated prompts.
replacements.after:
Table~\ref{tab:process-dynamics} shows that 74.6\% of traces are cycle-compliant with the \texttt{Planning}$\rightarrow$\texttt{Translating}$\rightarrow$\texttt{Reviewing} order, while a return from Review to Translating occurs in 14.8\% of runs.
Full replanning after Review is rare (0.3\%), as is replacing an existing goal (0.5\%), so our system uses its adaptive control more often for targeted redrafting than for full replanning.

replacements.instruction: Align the Figure 2 interpretation with the observed difference between targeted redrafting and full replanning while preserving the adaptive-ordering interpretation.
replacements.before: Our system mostly follows the same forward \texttt{Planning}$\rightarrow$\texttt{Translating}$\rightarrow$\texttt{Reviewing} progression as \condFixedOrder, with few departures to earlier processes; this concentration is consistent with the small exploratory advantage of adaptive ordering.
replacements.after: Our system mostly follows the same forward \texttt{Planning}$\rightarrow$\texttt{Translating}$\rightarrow$\texttt{Reviewing} progression as \condFixedOrder; returns to Translating are more common than returns to Planning, consistent with the small exploratory advantage of adaptive ordering.
